clue.text: Boxer who sat up after crumbling

indicators.note: something crumbling falls to pieces, so the letters of the words before it break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A fighter who got up off the canvas after collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' looks like the subject of the story; it is the definition, and 'who sat up' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer, leading with the right hand, is known in the ring by this nickname.

clue.text: 21 former duchy

parts.note: the answer to 21 across is see-through; to see through someone or something is to work it out, informally to suss it
a former partner is an ex

explanation.surface: A cross-reference describing a dukedom of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer at 21 across, which is then read as the verb 'see through', meaning to figure out. The county gives its name to the royal title Duke of Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county in the south gives its title to a royal dukedom, so it stands loosely for the duke's domain.

clue.text: Son trapped by loveless marriage unlikely to delete …

indicators.note: a thing trapped by others sits inside them, so the son letter goes between the pieces around it
love is nil in tennis, the letter O, and loveless says it is taken away

parts.note: a marriage is a union
an unlikely story is a tall one

explanation.surface: A son caught in a cold marriage is not going to wipe something out, the sentence trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, a nil score in tennis. The ellipsis carries the sentence on into 3 down, which is why the definition seems to lack an object.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove software from a computer is to wipe it away, a modern sense of erasing.

clue.text: … www.tinder.com, perhaps after hot fling

indicators.note: the web address piece comes after the hot letter in the answer

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a web address like this is an example of a URL

explanation.surface: Continuing 2 down: someone will not delete the dating app after a steamy fling.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this clue to 2 down as one sentence about a dating app; 'perhaps' marks the web address as an example of a URL.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling something is to throw it hard, which is a synonym of the answer as a verb.

clue.text: Chip, software, joint effort

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
a roach is the butt of a cannabis joint, so a joint can stand for it
to have a shot is to make an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A list that sounds like a computer chip, some software and a group effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chip' looks like a computer part beside 'software'; it is a golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a short lofted stroke onto the green is a chip, one kind of stroke played towards the flag.

clue.text: One's brace hurt

parts.note: one is can be said as I am, shortened to I'm
a brace is a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Someone's dental brace has caused them pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as possessive but stands for 'one is', said by oneself as I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or weaken something is to harm it, so the verb is a synonym of hurt.

clue.text: Gentleness of old chap, sort of fat and due for treatment

parts.note: a chap is a man
suet is a kind of hard animal fat used in cooking

indicators.note: something sent for treatment is worked on and changed, so the letters of due are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe-like list: an old fellow, some fat, and something due to be processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of old' belongs to the definition: the answer is an archaic word. 'and' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic word for meekness or tameness, now found mainly in old texts.

clue.text: Expert taped broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so the letters of taped are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist's recorded talk went out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone highly skilled at something is a master, matching the adjective or noun sense.

clue.text: Petra's colour returned in seaside resort

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters wanted sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A colour seen again on coming back to a beach town.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had no indicator for the hidden step; 'in' is that indicator, and 'returned' turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra in Jordan is called 'a rose-red city half as old as time' in a famous line of Victorian poetry.

clue.text: Where to put your feet up

definitions.text: Where to put your feet up

parts.words: Where to put your feet up
parts.note: reads as a place to relax, but means the loops a rider puts their feet in, held up off the ground

explanation.surface: An invitation to sit back and relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put your feet up' suggests resting; it is a rider's feet raised and held on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's feet rest in metal loops hung from the saddle, held up beside the horse.

clue.text: French city gets hot

definitions.meaning: a city on the Loire in western France
makes someone hot under the collar, that is enrages them

explanation.definitionFit: The Loire city shares its spelling with the verb meaning enrages, which is to make someone heated.

clue.text: Instruction for gro_e; there's a line for you to work out

definitions.text: there's a line for you to work out

indicators.note: the answer is to be read as an order which, carried out, turns a word into the fragment shown

parts.note: a word of five letters with its fourth letter blanked out by an underscore

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's note about a blank in a word, with a line to fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SKIP P IN GROPE, the answer is an order that turns grope into 'gro_e'. 'line' and 'work out' sound like puzzle-solving terms but mean a rope for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord swung over the head and jumped is a staple of gym workouts, a line used for exercise.

clue.text: Stand in front of painter, nearly still

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an easel is the stand an artist works at

explanation.surface: A model posing before an artist, almost motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as an adjective for the model; it is a verb meaning calm or soothe.
explanation.definitionFit: To still pain or worry is to relieve or calm it, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Stud flipping knackered by leading lady in this bestseller

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a stud or doorknob is a knob
knackered, broken, is bust in slang
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen, the leading lady of the land

explanation.surface: A racy blurb: a womaniser, utterly worn out by the heroine of this steamy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word but reverses KNOB. ER is a standard abbreviation for the Queen; 'by' and 'in' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular novel full of sex and glamour, of the sort that sells in huge numbers, is known by this slang term.

clue.text: Picture lovers breaking awkward silence with quiet greeting

indicators.note: the quiet greeting breaks into the middle of the jumbled letters, so it goes inside them
an awkward arrangement is a clumsy one, so the letters of silence are reshuffled

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Film fans ending an uncomfortable silence by saying a soft hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' scrambles SILENCE to CINELES, and 'breaking' splits it after the fourth letter to take PHI. P for quiet comes from musical notation (piano).
explanation.definitionFit: Film enthusiasts love the movies, informally called the pictures.

clue.text: Retired potter Charlie finished pot for Murray etc.

parts.note: Steve Davis is a retired snooker champion; snooker players pot balls
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
time is up when it has finished

explanation.surface: An ex-ceramicist named Charlie completes a vessel for a man called Murray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potter' suggests pottery but means a snooker player: Steve Davis was a world champion of the 1980s. 'pot' is slang for a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Murray and other tennis players compete for this international team trophy, a cup being a pot.

clue.text: When ordering taxi, cross here?

parts.note: reads like an instruction about hailing a cab, but asks where the cross, the letter X, stands in the spelling of the word taxi

explanation.surface: A question about where to cross the road when calling for a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' means putting the letters in order, and 'cross' is the letter X, which comes in place number three of T-A-X-I.
explanation.definitionFit: The X in the word comes after two letters, so its position is the ordinal after second.

clue.text: Like it mixed with ice and slice of lemon

indicators.note: a mixed drink is stirred together, so these letters are combined and rearranged
a slice is a small piece, here just the opening letter of the word lemon

explanation.surface: A cocktail order: shaken with ice and a slice of lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is not a link here: its letters go into the anagram with IT, ICE and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are alike in every respect are the same, so like and the answer are synonyms.

clue.text: Tear into two very fit guards

indicators.note: the outer word guards the other by surrounding it

parts.note: hale means healthy, fit

explanation.surface: A very fit pair of security guards tears something apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something into two equal parts is to split it down the middle.

clue.text: Belligerent publican on Lewis maybe ignoring Sabbath

parts.note: Lewis in the Outer Hebrides is an example of an isle

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis is a Scottish island famed for strict Sunday observance, which fits 'ignoring Sabbath'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive and unfriendly people are warlike in attitude, a synonym of belligerent.

clue.text: German with a list wants wife to replace central heating, sharp

indicators.note: one letter is to replace others, taking their place in the word

parts.note: Oskar Schindler, the German industrialist of the film Schindler's List

explanation.surface: A German with a list of jobs wants his wife to sort the boiler, sharpish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' is a noun here, a cheat, as in card sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp is a cheat or con man, as in card sharp, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Absent father meets your total indifference

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for absent, as on a register
pa is father
thy is an old form of your

explanation.surface: A neglectful dad meets someone who could not care less.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete lack of interest or concern is the meaning, a synonym of utter indifference.

clue.text: Those huge pants Romeo wears not hiding much

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wear the Romeo letter, holding it inside like a garment

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lover in very large underpants that reveal more than they should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear; in British slang it means rubbish, so it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric reveals what is beneath it, so it hides very little.

clue.text: Tanner, maybe in Spain, lies cooking

indicators.note: cooking the letters means doctoring them, so lies is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sunbather in Spain, perhaps, lying in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanner' looks like a sunbather; it is Elsie Tanner, a long-running character in the British TV soap Coronation Street. 'in' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie Tanner was a famous Coronation Street character, so the first name is one example of a Tanner.

clue.text: Pack it in jars to be sent back

parts.note: jars are pots

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack it in' looks like packing the jars; it is the idiom meaning quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack something in is to quit or give it up, so the phrase is an idiom for cease.

clue.text: A thousand extra at work

parts.note: a, as in ten pounds a day, means per

explanation.surface: An extra thousand pounds for doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit given on top of salary, such as a company car, is a perquisite of a job.

clue.text: Slight consequence of Chamberlain's ultimatum being largely ignored

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamberlain' suggests the British prime minister of 1938-40; the letters sit across 'Chamberlain's ultimatum'. 'consequence of' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or affront, so the noun is a synonym of an offensive remark.

clue.text: Might share when supply fails

parts.note: might is strength or power
a share of the takings is a cut

explanation.surface: Someone may share out what they have once supplies run short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like the verb 'may'; it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: An interruption to the electricity supply is a blackout, the moment when supply fails.

clue.text: Despite all that drawing, cartographers misdirected
